items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: I went with Burst Ketate at the Vendome at that time.

ctx.x: Well now as a trumpet player, did it give you more scope to play in a group like this?

Well, I didn't very much attention to the idea of, you know, what I was going to do. I went with so many different organizations. I went with Burst Ketate at the Vendome at that time. And as you go along, you know, you're changing styles. And I was playing for silent pictures, big old symphony orchestra playing for silent pictures. And after the curtain go up, you play on the chair and a hot number. That's where I came in, you know. And as the years go on, you lose a lot. It's impossible that you do that, you know.
But that was really the first thing that I lost the memory.
